text: The Aga Khan University Hospital (AKUH) is a private hospital located in Karachi, Pakistan, established in 1985 with a US$300 million investment from Prince Karim Aga Khan. The government of Muhammad Zia-ul-Haq provided an 84-acre site for the hospital at no cost. AKUH serves as the primary teaching hospital for the Aga Khan University's Faculty of Health Sciences and offers secondary and tertiary care, including disease diagnosis and team-based patient management. The hospital has 560 beds, comprising 122 private and 117 semi-private air-conditioned rooms, 251 General Ward beds, and 52 special care beds in the ICU, CCU, and NICU. It features 17 main operating theatres, 4 in Surgical Day Care, and 2 in Obs/Gyn Day Care, where day care surgeries are performed. AKUH provides a range of specialized services, including pharmacy, radiology (including nuclear medicine), laboratory, cardiopulmonary, neurophysiology, and physiological measurement. Its laboratory operates 47 phlebotomy or specimen collection centers across Karachi and all major cities in Pakistan. A new private wing was added to the hospital, with construction completed in 2020. The Aga Khan Medical Complex, situated on a 65-acre site in Karachi, was planned and designed by Payette Associates, a Boston-based architectural firm, and incorporates a 721-bed hospital, a medical school for 500 students, a school of nursing, staff and student housing, and a mosque. The complex is designed to reflect the history, climate, environment, symbolism, and spiritual values of Muslim culture. AKUH is accredited by both the Joint Commission International (JCI) and the College of Physicians and Surgeons of Pakistan. In 2017, a joint board was formed between AKUH and the Karachi Municipal Corporation (KMC) to study all major hospitals in Karachi and assist in upgrading KMC-affiliated medical facilities. AKUH is recognized as a leader in introducing new healthcare technology in Pakistan; in 2016, The Express Tribune reported that it became the first medical center in the country to introduce the Neuro-Robotic Exoscope, an advanced brain surgery technology. The hospital's geographic coordinates are 24°53′36″N 67°04′28″E (24.8933°N 67.0744°E).
